stem: Monthly service reviews raise a question about how AWS DataSync, AWS Transfer Family, and AWS Storage Gateway differ, before a recommendation is made for two upcoming projects. Select TWO accurate statements about these services. (Select TWO.)

choices.text: AWS Storage Gateway is billed per GB transferred with no appliance to run
AWS Transfer Family needs an EC2-hosted FTP server to operate
AWS DataSync provides managed SFTP and FTPS protocol endpoints
AWS Transfer Family provides managed SFTP, FTPS, and AS2 endpoints backed by S3 or EFS
AWS DataSync is billed per GB transferred with no appliance to run

rationale: AWS Transfer Family provides managed SFTP, FTPS, and AS2 endpoints backed by S3 or EFS, letting external partners exchange files without a self-managed server. AWS DataSync is billed per GB transferred with no gateway appliance to run, which is what makes it a low-cost choice for bulk transfers. AWS Storage Gateway runs a gateway appliance or virtual machine to provide its local cache, so it is not an appliance-free, per-GB transfer service. Transfer Family is specifically built to avoid standing up and patching an EC2-hosted FTP server, so needing one contradicts what it provides. Managed SFTP and FTPS endpoints are Transfer Family's role, not something AWS DataSync provides.
